import json,hashlib
O='products/services/software-renewals/integration/checks.json'
r=json.load(open(O,encoding='utf-8'))
new=open('products/sites/software-award-brief/index.html',encoding='utf-8').read()
old=new
for s in r['added_strings']: old=old.replace(s,'')
ok=hashlib.sha256(old.encode()).hexdigest()==r['hashes']['baseline_index']
k='site%3Asoftware-award-brief'
for c in r['checks']:
    if c['check']=='intake_mailto_unchanged':
        c.update({'pass':ok and new.count(k)==old.count(k)==2 and new.count('mailto:')==old.count('mailto:')==1,'note':'First run expected count 1 and failed; that expectation was wrong: the single mailto carries the identifier in subject and body (2 occurrences) in both baseline and candidate. Corrected check: counts equal (2) and exactly one mailto in both.','first_run_pass':False,'counts':{'baseline':old.count(k),'candidate':new.count(k)}})
r['all_pass']=all(c['pass'] for c in r['checks'])
r['candidate_index_sha256_recheck']=hashlib.sha256(new.encode()).hexdigest()
json.dump(r,open(O,'w',encoding='utf-8'),ensure_ascii=False,indent=1)
print(json.dumps({'all_pass':r['all_pass'],'reconstructed_baseline_ok':ok,'n':len(r['checks']),'failed':[c for c in r['checks'] if not c['pass']]}))
